record.paper_title: Collective Phenomena in the LiHoxY1−xF4 Quantum Ising Magnet: Recent Progress and Open Questions
record.original_question: For diluted dipolar Ising models intended to describe LiHoxY1−xF4, can larger classical Monte Carlo simulations bring finite-size corrections under control, reconcile the different spin-glass correlation-length crossings along the a and c axes, and thereby determine the finite-temperature spin-glass transition more reliably?

evidence.quote: In Ref. [82], a finite-size crossing of ξsg divided by the linear system size L, ξsg/L, is observed, providing good evidence for a finite temperature spin-glass transition, in agreement with the most recent AC susceptibility experiments [79].

However, the critical temperature determined by the crossing of ξsg/L is slightly different for ξsg along the a and c axes. This indicates that the finite size corrections to scaling are not under control for the system sizes considered and simulations on larger system sizes are therefore needed.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a site-diluted dipolar Ising model on a tetragonal lattice intended as a microscopic description of LiHo_xY_{1−x}F_4: place classical Ising spins σ_i = ±1 on a fraction x of the rare-earth sites of a tetragonal lattice (with distinct a and c crystallographic axes) and let them interact via the long-range, anisotropic magnetic dipole-dipole interaction (with appropriate Ewald summation under periodic boundary conditions), with the Ising axis aligned along the c axis. For a finite system of linear size L, define the wavevector-dependent spin-glass susceptibility from the disorder- and thermal-averaged squared overlap, and from it define the second-moment spin-glass correlation length ξ_sg(L,T) separately for wavevectors along the a and c axes, yielding ξ_sg^a(L,T) and ξ_sg^c(L,T).

It is known that, for accessible system sizes, the curves ξ_sg^a(L,T)/L for different L cross at one apparent temperature, while the curves ξ_sg^c(L,T)/L cross at a slightly different apparent temperature, suggesting that finite-size corrections to scaling are not yet under control.

Question: by performing classical Monte Carlo simulations on substantially larger system sizes L, can one bring the leading finite-size scaling corrections under control, force the crossing temperatures of ξ_sg^a/L and ξ_sg^c/L to coincide in the L → ∞ limit, and thereby reliably determine the finite-temperature spin-glass transition temperature T_sg(x) of this site-diluted dipolar Ising model?
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent Monte Carlo studies (e.g., Tam–Gingras and Alonso–Fernández type works on site-diluted dipolar Ising models, and later large-scale simulations of dipolar spin glasses in 3D published in Phys. Rev. B 100, 064425 (2019)) provide stronger evidence for a finite-temperature spin-glass transition and give critical exponents, but I did not find a clear, definitive resolution of the specific axis-dependent discrepancy between the ξ_sg^a/L and ξ_sg^c/L crossings for the realistic LiHo_xY_{1−x}F_4 model. Status appears unresolved/unclear from available sources.

status_evidence.title: Monte Carlo study of the spin-glass phase of the site-diluted dipolar Ising model
status_evidence.snippet: Tempered Monte Carlo simulations on cubic lattices examining ξ_L/L for site-diluted dipolar Ising spins.
status_evidence.claim: Earlier MC work establishing the ξ/L crossing methodology for diluted dipolar Ising systems.

status_evidence.title: Spin Glass Transition at Nonzero Temperature in a Disordered Dipolar Ising System: The Case of LiHoxY1-xF4
status_evidence.snippet: Evidence for a finite-temperature spin-glass transition in a microscopic model of LiHoxY1-xF4.
status_evidence.claim: Provides initial finite-temperature transition evidence but with axis-dependent crossings.

status_evidence.title: Dipolar spin glass transition in three dimensions, Phys. Rev. B 100, 064425
status_evidence.snippet: Large-scale simulations giving ν=1.27(8), η=0.228(35), supporting a finite-T spin-glass transition in dilute dipolar Ising systems.
status_evidence.claim: Later, larger-scale simulations strengthen evidence for the transition but study an anisotropic dilute dipolar model rather than directly resolving the LiHoxY1-xF4 a-vs-c crossing discrepancy.
